scope: Public-safe citation and inference review for the report revision. No new omics analysis, treatment action or publication is performed by this review.

review_access.independent_review_scope: Antigen-selection/bottleneck sections and cited primary clinical studies; full16-page primary review and figure inspection already documented in the prior audit
review_access.primary_evidence_basis: Targeted 18 November primary-source checks supplemented by the independently reviewed 17 November full-paper clinical audit. Same-day access statuses retained from the current public source; no redundant broad trial search.

overall_assessment: The review strengthens attention to antigen quality, coordinated priming and recruitment. It does not validate the exact proposed regimen, establish the dominant present-lesion mechanism, or justify increasing existing axis confidence solely from biological plausibility.

report_ready_corrections.report_text: Dendritic cells must present the vaccine with appropriate activation to prime T cells. Direct CD8 killing then requires the cancer cell to naturally display the matching peptide–HLA class I complex. Improving the first step does not prove or repair the second. CD4 helper activity can operate through antigen-presenting cells without requiring malignant-cell HLA class II.

Prioritise retained clonal mutations, actual mutant-transcript expression, correctly phased sequences, multiple HLA alleles and demonstrable CD4/CD8 coverage. Whole-gene TPM and predicted HLA binding cannot establish mutant-peptide production or natural cancer recognition; more peptides do not guarantee effective breadth.

FLT3 ligand expands DC populations; CD40 and innate adjuvants supply activation/priming signals. N-803 predominantly supports NK/CD8 lymphocytes. These are complementary biological steps, not interchangeable drugs. Expansion alone cannot establish DC function, intratumour entry or cancer-cell antigen display.

Archival DC-associated markers are mixed, not proof of global DC absence. Low chemokines support a recruitment hypothesis, but cause and consequence remain unresolved. Caris versus resection antigen-display results are heterogeneous; retained bulk HLA-related proteins do not prove malignant-cell display in a current node.

Blood vaccine-specific responses, NK expansion and TCR-clone expansion are useful pharmacodynamic observations, not validated surrogates for tumour control. Low-volume active metastases should not be described as the completely resected setting of positive adjuvant vaccine trials.

Antigen delivery, DC activation and checkpoint timing require coordinated clinical planning. The review describes context-dependent approaches; preclinical sequencing findings do not define a universal human schedule.

The four-part proposal is biologically coherent but has no established efficacy, safety or schedule as a complete regimen. The Nature review does not directly test vactosertib or N-803. Neither stronger mechanistic coverage nor adding a fifth agent establishes clinical benefit.

The current commercial Anktiva label is for intravesical use with BCG in BCG-unresponsive NMIBC and explicitly excludes subcutaneous, intravenous and intramuscular administration. Systemic N-803 in CRC remains investigational; clinicians must establish an appropriate product, route, access pathway and combination protocol. Commercial availability alone is not proof of injectable suitability.

clinical_evidence.design: Randomized phase II in high-risk resected melanoma; anti-DEC205/NY-ESO-1 vaccine plus poly-ICLC, with or without CDX-301.
clinical_evidence.finding: DC populations and antigen-specific humoral/T-cell responses increased. The principal endpoint was immunogenicity.
clinical_evidence.limit: No established clinical-benefit superiority, CRC efficacy, or case-specific response biomarker. Expansion still requires productive activation and antigen presentation.

clinical_evidence.design: Local CDX-1140 plus helper peptides and poly-ICLC in the adjuvant melanoma setting; single-arm early trial.
clinical_evidence.finding: No dose-limiting or grade 3+ treatment-related events reported. Six of 22 had an ex-vivo response to the six-helper-peptide pool; only one had a durable/persistent response.
clinical_evidence.limit: The separate mutant-BRAF response was detected after in-vitro stimulation, not ex vivo. Historical IFA-based studies had greater response rates, but that comparison is not randomized. Local tolerability does not establish systemic combination safety.

clinical_evidence.design: Synthetic long peptides with poly-ICLC, Montanide and vaccine-site ipilimumab plus systemic nivolumab; melanoma.
clinical_evidence.finding: One of the two vaccinated participants with unresectable disease progressed; the other changed from stable disease on nivolumab to partial then complete response after vaccination. No grade 3/4 dose-limiting vaccine toxicity reported.
clinical_evidence.limit: Predominantly resected-disease cohort, small and uncontrolled. Cannot isolate the contribution of Montanide or local ipilimumab, infer CRC benefit, or support systemic BOT/BAL rechallenge. Poly-ICLC is already intended in the current proposal.

clinical_evidence.design: Single-centre phase I/II refractory pMMR metastatic colorectal/appendiceal cohort; shared CEA/MUC1 viral vaccine, N-803 and bintrafusp, with/without targeted IL12.
clinical_evidence.finding: Median PFS 1.8 months in both cohorts. Sole response became complete and lasted29.2 months; the responder was checkpoint-naive with nodes-only disease after prior liver resection.
clinical_evidence.limit: Close mechanistic caution, not a test of personalised neoantigens plus vactosertib/PD1. Prior checkpoint participants are documented in Table 2 despite the abstract, but totals are internally inconsistent; do not quote a precise prior-ICI denominator. No grade 4/5 treatment-related events reported.

clinical_evidence.design: Nonrandomized phase Ib ALT-803 plus nivolumab in previously treated NSCLC.
clinical_evidence.finding: Exploratory post-hoc responses accompanied NK/CD8 pharmacodynamic effects.
clinical_evidence.limit: Small non-CRC study, not evidence for the full four-component proposal or a personal response rate. Response confirmation/analysis design limits must be retained.

clinical_evidence.design: Phase I advanced solid tumours; no CRC cohort.
clinical_evidence.finding: NK-cell expansion without objective tumour responses.
clinical_evidence.limit: Demonstrates that lymphocyte expansion alone does not guarantee tumour control; does not preclude a useful combination.

clinical_evidence.design: Randomized double-blind phase III after complete resection of stage IIB–IV cutaneous melanoma.
clinical_evidence.finding: At 24 months, recurrence-free survival 82.2% versus 70.0% (P<0.001); distant-metastasis-free survival 88.5% versus 80.2% (P=0.002). Grade 3+ adverse events 23.6% versus 20.3% were all-cause, not treatment-related.
clinical_evidence.limit: Supports clinical benefit in resected melanoma. Active low-volume metastatic CRC is not postoperative minimal residual disease; no platform superiority or benefit from the proposed additional agents follows.

clinical_evidence.design: Randomized phase II advanced melanoma; autogene cevumeran plus pembrolizumab versus pembrolizumab.
clinical_evidence.finding: Median PFS 8.3 versus 7.9 months, HR 0.78, P=0.3061; ORR 41.7% versus 48.8%.
clinical_evidence.limit: Primary conference result illustrates that immunogenicity is not a surrogate for improved tumour control. Different disease/platform; does not establish universal vaccine failure.

clinical_evidence.design: Open-label phase Ib/IIa vactosertib plus pembrolizumab; prior checkpoint therapy excluded.
clinical_evidence.finding: CRC ORR 12.6%, median PFS 1.2 months; responder median duration 12.5 months. Overall grade 3+ treatment-related events 22/120, including one possibly related sudden death.
clinical_evidence.limit: Not all 103 were confirmed MSS; prior BOT/BAL limits extrapolation. Four prespecified programmes in the 28-sample secondary RNA analysis had no significant clinical-benefit association (all BH q=0.521); this supplies no positive selector and does not exclude benefit.

integration_requirements: Preserve the relative confidence/order of the 9 case axes; add 5 research leads within the relevant priming/recruitment discussion without mechanistic efficacy bonuses.
Retain the completed 28-sample null-association findings and their limitations.
Keep public access status dated and distinguish an enquiry route from actual drug supply/approval.
Do not reintroduce organoid or tissue-culture proposals. Available-data target review and clinician-led blood/disease monitoring can be discussed with feasibility limits.
Do not publish full papers, emails, addresses, private IDs or unreviewed provider records.
Do not copy older historical website package snapshots as though they describe the current proposal.

metabolic_subreview.assessment: Both new metabolic-lead entries are broadly accurate. Preserve the drug/model distinctions and clarify the experimental DC interventions and study denominators.

metabolic_corrections.report_text: BAY-8002 rescued glycan-conditioned human dendritic-cell functions in laboratory experiments using healthy-donor cells. This is not systemic AZD3965 treatment or demonstrated tumour-antigen-specific vaccine efficacy; it does not establish a measured CRC lactate-flux defect.

AZD3965 escalation enrolled 42 and treated 40, including 20 enrolled with CRC. Of 39 with baseline disease assessment, nine had stable disease and nine lacked evaluable follow-up; no objective responses were reported. Retinal-test changes, troponin elevation and acidosis constrain extrapolation.

The BSO mouse study used spontaneous Grm1 melanoma with Flt3L and intratumoral poly(I:C)/anti-CD40 to expand and activate DCs; it was not an antigen-loaded DC vaccine. Direct tumour ferroptosis and other effects mean selective DC metabolic restoration is unproven.

Human BSO experience includes melphalan and stem-cell-supported neuroblastoma: 31 enrolled, 28 dose-evaluable, 25 response-evaluable, two partial and five mixed responses. Mixed response is not objective partial response. Combination toxicity cannot be attributed wholly to BSO; fatal toxicities discussed from an earlier pilot must not be assigned to this cohort.
